about: Questions a maintenance engineer could ask of FAA AC 43.13-1B (with Change 1). Each lists the PDF page(s) that actually answer it and 'facts': short phrases from the manual that the answer needs, both checked against the extracted text of the file fetched by scripts/fetch_sample_docs.ps1 (every fact sits inside one chunk on its page). 'pages' are PDF file page numbers (what a PDF viewer calls page N); 'labels' are the page numbers printed on those pages, for humans. A retrieved chunk counts as a hit when it comes from one of these pages; a fact counts as found when its text appears in a chunk the model would read (case and spacing ignored). 'off_topic' questions have no answer in the manual and must be refused: the first three are generic, the rest are aviation questions that this manual does not cover (checked: none of their key terms occur in it), which is the harder test for MAX_DISTANCE. Each off_topic entry has a 'kind': 'generic' (not aviation), 'outside' (aviation the manual does not cover; its key terms do not occur) or 'near_topic' (the manual covers the subject and uses its words, but not the specific figure or procedure asked for; 'manual_says' records what it does say, checked against the extracted text 2026-10-18). Near-topic questions pass the distance gate by design: they test the answer check and prompt rule 2, not MAX_DISTANCE. Entries with "author": "user" (added 2026-10-19) were written by the project owner, not by the author of the checker: broad, section-level questions whose answer spans several pages, so 'pages' lists every page that answers part of it and 'facts' are a few of the key phrases, each checked to sit whole in one chunk (paragraph chunking) on a listed page.

items.question: How is a critical fatigue area defined for aircraft control cables?
facts: runs over, under, or around a pulley
within 1 foot of a swaged-on fitting

items.question: How do I find broken wires in a control cable during an inspection?
facts: passing a cloth over the area
magnifying glass of 7 power

items.question: When must a kinked control cable or one with a popped core be replaced?
facts: in a kinked cable, strands and wires are out of position
replace any cable that has a popped core

items.question: How much can the outer wires of a control cable wear before the cable has to be replaced?
facts: 40 to 50 percent

items.question: What proof load is used to test cable terminals and splices before installation?
facts: 60 percent of the cable breaking strengths
3 minutes

items.question: What is the minimum edge distance and spacing for a single row of rivets?
facts: not be less than 2 times the diameter
3 times the diameter

items.question: What slope is the steepest allowed for a scarf patch in a plywood skin?
facts: scarf slope of 1 in 12

items.question: After safetying a turnbuckle, how many threads of the terminal may still show?
facts: no more than three threads

items.question: What resistance must the electrical bond between a piece of equipment and the aircraft structure have?
facts: less than 2.5 milliohms

items.question: What is galvanic corrosion and how can I recognise it?
facts: two dissimilar metals make contact
buildup of corrosion at the joint

items.question: What does exfoliation corrosion look like and where does it usually show up?

items.question: Why does heated titanium change colour, and should the coloured film be removed?
facts: blue oxide coating
should not be removed

items.question: Which torque values do I use for nuts and bolts when the manufacturer gives none?
facts: when specific torque is not supplied by the manufacturer

items.question: Can a metal fuel tank be welded or soldered, and what has to be done first?
facts: must not be welded or soldered
adequately purged

items.question: How far apart can clamps be when supporting wires and cables in an aircraft?
facts: not more than 24 inches

items.question: Which gas is recommended for inflating aircraft tires, and which must never be used?
facts: use of nitrogen to inflate tires is recommended
do not use oxygen to inflate tires

items.question: Why is it dangerous to service lead-acid and nickel-cadmium batteries in the same area?
facts: extremely dangerous to store or service lead-acid and nicad batteries

items.question: Which materials can be checked with magnetic particle inspection?
facts: ferromagnetic materials (iron and steel)

items.question: How reliable is a mechanical punch tester for judging the condition of aircraft fabric?
facts: punch test accuracy will depend

items.question: How should oxygen and fuel gas cylinders be secured in a welding area?
facts: secure oxygen and fuel gas cylinders

items.question: How long may an abrasive blast stream stay on one spot of an aluminium skin?
facts: longer than 15 seconds

items.question: What is the empty weight center of gravity of an aircraft?
facts: the empty weight center of gravity (ewcg) is the cg of an aircraft

off_topic.question: what is the capital of France?
give me a recipe for a chocolate cake
how do I configure an ingress controller in Kubernetes?
What is the maximum takeoff weight of an Airbus A320?
How do I jack up a Boeing 737 to change a main wheel?
How do I load a flight plan into a Garmin G1000?
What are the rules for dispatching with an inoperative item under the minimum equipment list?
How do I replace the fan blades on a GE90 turbofan engine?
How is a cabin pressurization outflow valve adjusted on an airliner?
How do I repair a carbon fiber propeller blade?
off_topic.manual_says: Propeller repairs cover wood and metal blades; the composite repairs exclude 'advanced composite components, such as graphite (carbon fiber)'. No carbon blade repair.

off_topic.question: What torque applies to a helicopter main rotor blade bolt?
off_topic.manual_says: Torque is covered generally (Table 7-1 when the manufacturer gives none); nothing on helicopter rotor blade bolts.

off_topic.question: What gap should the electrodes of an aircraft spark plug be set to?
off_topic.manual_says: 8-15: check 'the proper gap setting' with a feeler gauge; regapping is in the manufacturers' manuals. No gap value.

off_topic.question: What pressure should the main landing gear tires of a light aircraft be inflated to?
off_topic.manual_says: 9-15: inflate to 'the recommended pressure'; nitrogen recommended. No pressure value.

off_topic.question: What nitrogen pressure should a nose gear shock strut be serviced to?
off_topic.manual_says: Landing gear: 'service the strut with nitrogen to get the proper strut extension'. No pressure.

off_topic.question: What tension should the aileron control cables be rigged to?
off_topic.manual_says: 7-153: adjust tension 'in accordance with the airframe manufacturer's recommendations'. No tension value.

off_topic.question: After how many hours of cumulative use must an ELT battery be replaced?
off_topic.manual_says: 12-22: inspect for corrosion, verify the battery is approved and check its expiration date. No hours.

off_topic.question: What is the time between overhaul for a Lycoming O-360 engine?
off_topic.manual_says: No TBO anywhere; Lycoming appears once, in a cylinder oversize table.

off_topic.question: What is the maximum RPM drop allowed when checking each magneto during the engine run-up?
off_topic.manual_says: No magneto drop limit; the only magneto RPM figure is a 1200 rpm troubleshooting run (a trap).

off_topic.question: What static RPM should a fixed-pitch propeller reach during a ground run-up?
off_topic.manual_says: No static RPM figure.

off_topic.question: What is the maximum allowable runout of a brake disk?
off_topic.manual_says: Brake disks: replace if cracked, warped, corroded or discolored. No runout limit (the word does not occur).

off_topic.question: What air pressure inflates the rubber deicer boots on a wing leading edge?
off_topic.manual_says: Deicer boots appear once, in a history note on engine discharge air. No pressure.

off_topic.question: How many months can prepreg fabric be stored in a freezer before it expires?
off_topic.manual_says: Composites: 'observe shelf life' of prepreg. No storage time or temperature.

off_topic.question: What is the glass transition temperature of a typical epoxy laminating resin?
off_topic.manual_says: Epoxy pot life and cure times are mentioned; 'glass transition' does not occur.

off_topic.question: How deep may corrosion pitting be on a wing spar cap before the spar must be replaced?
off_topic.manual_says: Corrosion chapter describes pitting and its removal; no pit-depth limit for spar caps.

off_topic.question: After how many years must aircraft seat belts be replaced?
off_topic.manual_says: Seat belts: TSO approval; replace when found unairworthy; webbing deteriorates. No age limit.

off_topic.question: How often must the discharge cartridge on an engine fire extinguisher bottle be replaced?
off_topic.manual_says: Cartridge-actuated extinguishers appear only in a wiring (shielding) paragraph. No replacement interval.

off_topic.question: How many flight hours are allowed between oil changes on a piston aircraft engine?
off_topic.manual_says: Oil changes are mentioned only for oil sampling and filter inspection. No interval.

off_topic.question: What is the maximum dent depth allowed on a turbine engine compressor blade?
off_topic.manual_says: 'Compressor blade' does not occur; turbine engines are barely covered.

off_topic.author: user
off_topic.question: What procedure does it give for repairing a delamination in a specific modern carbon-fiber aircraft panel?
off_topic.manual_says: The fiberglass repairs in chapter 3 (page 3-1) are 'not to be used on radomes or advanced composite components, such as graphite (carbon fiber) or kevlar'. No carbon-fiber panel delamination procedure.

off_topic.author: user
off_topic.question: What is the approved repair for a cracked wing spar on a particular aircraft, given its make, model, serial number, and damage location?
off_topic.manual_says: General wood spar splicing (1-40) and replacement (1-41, a major repair); repairs near bolt holes need approval from the manufacturer or the FAA (1-25). Nothing aircraft-specific.

off_topic.author: user
off_topic.question: What exact torque value should be used for a particular fastener in a specific aircraft installation?
off_topic.manual_says: Table 7-1 gives general torque values for when the manufacturer gives none; the value for a specific installation comes from the manufacturer. Borderline: a good answer points to the manufacturer and offers Table 7-1 only as the fallback.

off_topic.author: user
off_topic.question: Does the circular address whether a proposed repair complies with the latest airworthiness directive or other current requirement for a particular aircraft?
off_topic.manual_says: ADs appear only as a source of inspection requirements (5-1), in propeller notes (8-47) and the glossary; the AC does not determine AD compliance for a particular aircraft.
